blocks.text: **The problem.** Given an array `preorder` holding the **pre-order** walk (node, left subtree, right subtree) of a binary search tree with distinct values, rebuild the tree and return its root. A BST is fully determined by its pre-order.

blocks.alt: The pre-order 8, 5, 1, 7, 10, 12. The first value, 8, is the root. Everything after it that is smaller than 8, which is 5, 1 and 7, forms the left subtree; the rest, 10 and 12, forms the right subtree. Repeating this gives the tree 8, 5, 10, 1, 7, null, 12.

elements.text: first value = root; smaller values = left subtree; bigger = right
elements.originalText: first value = root; smaller values = left subtree; bigger = right

blocks.text: Pre-order lists every parent before its children. So inserting the values one by one with plain BST insertion puts each node exactly where it was.
**Time O(n·h)** — O(n²) for a skewed tree — **space O(h).**
2. One pass with an upper bound

Read the array left to right with a shared index. A call builds the subtree whose values are all below `bound`: if the next value is above the bound, this subtree is empty. Otherwise take it as the node, build its left subtree with bound = the node's value, and its right subtree with the parent's bound.

blocks.caption: Each value is taken once; a value above the current bound means "this subtree is finished".

blocks.code:
def bst_from_preorder(preorder):
    i = 0

    def build(bound):                     # the next subtree: values below bound
        nonlocal i
        if i == len(preorder) or preorder[i] > bound:
            return None
        node = TreeNode(preorder[i])
        i += 1
        node.left = build(node.val)       # smaller than this node
        node.right = build(bound)         # bigger than it, but still below bound
        return node

    return build(float("inf"))

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(h).** Every value is read exactly once.

Walk the values with a stack of the current path. A value smaller than the top is the top's **left** child. A bigger value pops every node smaller than it — the last one popped is its **parent**, and it becomes that parent's right child.
**Time O(n)** — each node is pushed and popped at most once — **space O(h).**

blocks.alt: Insert one by one: O(n·h) time, O(h) space. Upper bound, one pass: O(n) time, O(h) space. Monotonic stack: O(n) time, O(h) space.

items: **Increasing pre-order** — a right chain; the stack approach pops one node per value.
**Construct BST from postorder** — read from the end with a lower bound, building the right subtree first.
**Verify Preorder Sequence in BST** — run approach 3 and fail when a value is below the last popped node.
**Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder** — for a general tree you need the in-order too; a BST's in-order is just the sorted values.
